# 2c Expiry, shared-link alerts, dashboard: contract

**Read first:** [build README → Phase 2](./README.md#phase-2-subscriptions), [link lifecycle → expiry](../processes/subscriptions/link-lifecycle.md#steps--expiry-the-expiry-scan-every-15-min), [shared-link alerts](../processes/subscriptions/shared-link-alerts.md), [subscription format → app detection](../integrations/subscription-format.md#app-detection), [events → Subscriptions](../events.md#subscriptions), [notifications](../processes/platform/notifications.md), [jobs](../processes/platform/jobs.md) (schedules, quiet jobs, coalescing), designs `RP-Link` (the alert band, "Who fetches it"), `RP-Links`, `RP-Main` (the Links area), and the **As built** of 2a and 2b, and of 1f (schedules and quiet check jobs are the model).

**Done when:** a scan every 15 minutes warns once before a link expires, notifies once when it has expired, erases tombstoned tokens once their tombstone period ends and prunes old fetches; a scan every 15 minutes raises at most one shared-link alert per link per day over the per-link or global limits; the link page shows the alert, who fetches the link over 24 h and 7 d (networks with their country, apps) and lets the admin raise the limits or mute; network countries are looked up in the background; the dashboard has a Links area; Settings → Subscriptions exists; the notifications read well in both languages; every checklist line has its test.

## Decisions

| Topic | Decision | Why |
|---|---|---|
| Expiry scan | Job type `subscriptions.expiry_scan`: queue `maintenance`, `MaxAttempts 1`, `Quiet`, no resource key, steps `expiry`, `tombstones`, `prune`. Schedule `subscriptions.expiry_scan`: every 15 min, jitter 1 min. Each step calls a `links.Service` method that takes `now` (`ExpiryStep`, `TombstoneStep`, `PruneStep`), so tests call them directly with a time. | link-lifecycle.md "the expiry scan, every 15 min". |
| `expiry` step | One `Write`. (1) Active links with `expires_at ≤ now` and `expired_at` NULL → `expired_at = now`, `link.expired{expiry}`. (2) Active links with `now < expires_at ≤ now + subscriptions.expiry_warning` and `expiry_warned_at` NULL → `expiry_warned_at = now`, `link.expiring_soon{expiry}`. (1) runs first, so a link that expires before it was warned gets only `link.expired`. Disabled and deleted links are skipped: a disabled link that expires notifies nothing until it is enabled (then the next scan sends `link.expired`). 2b already re-arms both marks when the expiry changes. | Edge cases "once", "not repeated". |
| `tombstones` step | Deleted links with `deleted_at ≤ now − subscriptions.tombstone` and a token → `token`, `token_lookup` = NULL. No event: the URL already answers `404` from that moment (2b checks the clock), so nothing changes for anyone. The link's row and page stay. | link-lifecycle.md step 4; "bookkeeping that changes no behaviour records nothing". |
| `prune` step | Deletes fetches older than `subscriptions.fetch_retention` (default 90 days), network rows with a country older than `store.CountryFresh` (30 days) and rows without one older than `store.CountryRetry` (1 day), so a network still in use is looked up again. | shared-link-alerts.md "kept 90 days". |
| Counting | For a link and a window ending now: **networks** = distinct `network`; **apps** = distinct `app`, where an unknown app counts by its user agent (`CASE WHEN app = '' THEN 'ua:' \|\| user_agent ELSE app END`). Every outcome counts (stubs too). The window is `(now − 24 h, now]`. One grouped query serves the scan (all links at once) and the page (one link). | shared-link-alerts.md step 1 and rules. |
| Shared scan | Job type `subscriptions.shared_scan`: `maintenance`, `MaxAttempts 1`, `Quiet`, step `scan` (`alerts.Service.Scan(ctx, now, actor)`). Schedule every 15 min, jitter 1 min. For each link with fetches in the window (any state, deleted ones within their tombstone included): limits = the link's overrides, else `subscriptions.alert_networks` / `alert_apps`; over = networks **>** limit or apps **>** limit; alert when over, not muted, and `alerted_at` is NULL or at least 24 h old → `alerted_at = now`, `link.shared_suspected{networks, apps, window: "24h"}` (actor `job:<id>`). A link without fetches in the window isn't looked at. | shared-link-alerts.md steps. |
| "Has an alert" | A link alerted within the last 24 h and not muted. Shown as the gold triangle "looks shared" in the Links list and on the link page, counted in the list's status line, filtered by the chip **With alerts**, listed on the dashboard. | The design's marker. |
| Alert band | On the link page while it has an alert: a gold band "Shared-link alert · today 11:15" with the counts **as they are now** ("Fetched from 6 networks and 4 apps in the last 24 h. The limits are more than 4 networks or more than 3 apps."), "One person's devices rarely explain that. The URL has probably been passed on.", and **Regenerate token…**, **Disable…**, **Raise limits**, **Mute alerts**, each with its one-line consequence. (2d adds **Cut off …**.) | shared-link-alerts.md step 3; `RP-Link`. |
| Who fetches it | An area with a 24 h / 7 d switch (`?window=7d`; `.pc-sb`): **Networks · N** (network, country, fetches; most fetches first) and **Apps · N** (family or "Other: <user agent>", fetches). Shown even when muted ("The counts still show on its page"). The **Link** area gains "Alert limits: defaults · more than 4 networks or 3 apps in 24 h" (or the overrides, or "muted"). | shared-link-alerts.md edge case "muted … counts still show". |
| Raise limits, mute | `GET`/`POST /links/:id/alerts`: a page styled as a dialog with networks and apps (empty = the setting, 1–1 000) and **Mute alerts for this link**. **Mute alerts** in the band posts `muted=1` directly; the page has **Unmute**. Each change records `link.changed{fields}` with `alert limits` and/or `alerts muted`. Raising the limits does not clear `alerted_at`. | shared-link-alerts.md "Raise limits", "Mute". |
| Network countries | `subscriptions.network_country_url` (2a; default `https://ipinfo.io/{ip}/country`, empty = off). The fetch's `Write` (2b's recording) also, when the setting is not empty and the network has no row in `subs_network_countries`, enqueues `subscriptions.network_countries` with coalescing key `network-countries` (later fetches merge into the queued job). Job: `maintenance`, `MaxAttempts 1`, `Quiet`, step `lookup`: the networks seen in fetches of the last 7 days that have no row (stale rows are deleted by the expiry scan's `prune` step), at most 50 per run; for each, `geoip.Lookup(ctx, pattern, first address of the network)` (`198.51.100.0`, `2001:db8:4f2::`; never a client's own address), then one `Write` upserting the rows (`country` or `''`). Pages join the rows to show a country next to each network and fetch. | User default (build README); one look-up per network a month. |
| geoip | `internal/modules/servers/geoip` moves to `internal/platform/geoip` unchanged (`git mv`; servers' `provision/form.go` and the test import the new path). Both modules use it; neither imports the other's packages. | ADR 0002. |
| Fetch log | Gains the country column (from the network's row; `—` when unknown). | |
| Dashboard | `DashboardDeclarer`, one area **Links** (order 30, after servers' 20) with **Links →**: links with an alert ("Alex · alert · 6 networks, 4 apps in 24 h") and active links expiring within 7 days and not yet expired ("Masha — Pixel · expiring · 9 Oct · in 4 days"), alerts first. Nothing to show → no area. | ui/README dashboard "Links"; `RP-Main`. |
| Notifications | `NotificationRenderer` for `link.expiring_soon` (its title names the date: `ShortDate(expires − 1 s)` in the admin's language and zone) and `link.expired` (the same for the day it expired). The others use the default (`notify.<type>`, `.body`, payload fields, `{subject}`). Texts below. | events.md "Notification behaviour". |
| Settings page | `SettingsPageDeclarer`: `{Slug: "subscriptions", Title: "settings.subscriptions", Order: 36}`; `GET`/`POST /settings/subscriptions` with `ui.SettingsLayout` + `ui.SettingsForm` for section `subscriptions` (2a's seven keys, each with label and help), like `/settings/servers`. The country URL's help: "Proxier sends the first address of each network that fetched a link (never the person's own address). Empty turns countries off." | 2a registered the section. |

Notification texts (EN; each has its RU twin):

| Event | Emoji | Title | Sentence |
|---|---|---|---|
| `link.expiring_soon` | ⏳ | {subject} expires on {date} | Extend it on its page if it should keep working. |
| `link.expired` | ⏳ | {subject} expired on {date} | Its app gets the “expired” entry on its next refresh. |
| `link.shared_suspected` | 🟡 | {subject} looks shared | Fetched from {networks} networks and {apps} apps in 24 h. |
| `subscription.all_unhealthy` | 🟡 | Every server of {subject} is unhealthy | Hiding them would leave nothing, so all {count} are served. |

The notification never names an IP (shared-link-alerts.md rules); the button opens the link or subscription page.

## Go signatures

```go
package links
func (s *Service) ExpiryStep(ctx context.Context, now time.Time, actor string) error
func (s *Service) TombstoneStep(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) error
func (s *Service) PruneStep(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) error
func (s *Service) JobType() jobs.Type     // subscriptions.expiry_scan
func (s *Service) Schedule() jobs.Schedule

package alerts
const Window = 24 * time.Hour
type Count struct {
	Key     string // a network, or an app family / "ua:<user agent>"
	Country string // networks only; "" unknown
	Fetches int
}
type Counts struct{ Networks, Apps []Count } // most fetches first
type Limits struct {
	Networks, Apps int
	Muted          bool
	Default        bool // both come from the settings
}
type Service struct{ /* DB, Events, Settings, Jobs, Now, Log */ }
func (s *Service) Counts(ctx context.Context, linkID int64, since time.Time) (Counts, error)
func (s *Service) Limits(ctx context.Context, l links.Link) (Limits, error)
func (s *Service) HasAlert(l links.Link, now time.Time) bool
func (s *Service) Scan(ctx context.Context, now time.Time, actor string) error
func (s *Service) SetLimits(ctx context.Context, linkID int64, networks, apps int, muted bool, actor string) error // 0 = the setting
func (s *Service) LookupCountries(ctx context.Context, now time.Time) error // the job's step
func (s *Service) JobTypes() []jobs.Type   // subscriptions.shared_scan, subscriptions.network_countries
func (s *Service) Schedules() []jobs.Schedule
// QueueCountry enqueues the lookup inside the fetch's transaction when the
// network has no row and lookups are on.
func (s *Service) QueueCountry(ctx context.Context, tx *sqlx.Tx, network string) error

package store
const (
	CountryFresh   = 30 * 24 * time.Hour
	CountryRetry   = 24 * time.Hour
)

package substest
// StartJobs runs the job workers with fast polls until the test ends; Drain
// waits until no job is queued or running (serverstest's are the model).
func (h *Harness) StartJobs()
func (h *Harness) Drain()
// FetchAt inserts a fetch row directly (link, time, IP, user agent), with the
// network and app computed as a real fetch would: the alert tests place
// fetches at exact times without going through HTTP.
func (h *Harness) FetchAt(linkID int64, at time.Time, ip, ua string)
```

## Routes

| Method, path | What |
|---|---|
| `GET /links/:id?window=7d` | The link page with "Who fetches it" over 7 days |
| `GET`, `POST /links/:id/alerts` | Raise limits, mute, unmute |
| `GET /links?alerts=1` | The **With alerts** chip |
| `GET`, `POST /settings/subscriptions` | Settings → Subscriptions |

## Events

Recorded: `link.expiring_soon`, `link.expired`, `link.shared_suspected`, `link.changed` (alert limits, alerts muted).

## Doc changes in the same commit

- `docs/processes/subscriptions/link-lifecycle.md` (expiry scan): the step order (expired first), disabled links notify nothing, tombstone erasure records no event, the scan also prunes fetches.
- `docs/processes/subscriptions/shared-link-alerts.md`: the counts on the band are current; "has an alert" is "alerted within 24 h, not muted"; raising limits doesn't clear the alert; countries come from looking up each network's first address once a month (setting, empty turns it off).
- `docs/events.md`: the notification texts table above.
- `docs/modules/subscriptions.md`: Settings → Subscriptions; the dashboard's Links area.
- `docs/data-model.md#retention`: fetches kept `subscriptions.fetch_retention` (default 90 days); network countries kept 30 days (unknown ones retried after a day); tombstones last `subscriptions.tombstone` (default 30 days).
- `docs/architecture.md#outbound-connections`: the country lookup of fetch networks.

## Checklist

Expiry scan, in `links/scan_test.go`:

- [x] Expiry within 3 days → one `link.expiring_soon`; the next scans don't repeat it — `TestExpiringSoonOnce`
- [x] Past its expiry → one `link.expired`, also across later scans; the fetch already served the stub before the scan ran — `TestExpiredOnce`
- [x] An expiry extended to another date within 3 days → warned again — `TestExtendingWarnsAgain`
- [x] A disabled link that expires → no `link.expired`; enabled later → `link.expired` at the next scan — `TestDisabledLinkExpiresQuietly`
- [x] A link deleted 31 days ago → its token and lookup erased, its URL `404`s, its page still opens; no event — `TestTombstoneTokenErased`
- [x] Fetches older than `subscriptions.fetch_retention` are deleted, newer ones kept (at the default 90 days and with 30 days set) — `TestFetchRetention`
- [x] The schedule is declared every 15 minutes; the job, queued with `EnqueueNow` and drained, runs its three steps and succeeds — `TestExpiryScanJob`

Shared-link alerts, in `alerts/scan_test.go` (fetch rows inserted at chosen times):

- [x] One phone fetching from 10 addresses of one /24 → 1 network, no alert — `TestSameNetworkCountsOnce`
- [x] Fetches from 5 different /24 networks in 24 h → an alert (more than 4) — `TestFiveNetworksAlert`
- [x] 4 networks and 4 apps (Happ, v2RayTun, Hiddify, Shadowrocket) → an alert (more than 3 apps) — `TestFourAppsAlert`
- [x] An alert at 10:00, still over at 10:15 → no second alert until 10:00 the next day — `TestOneAlertPerDay`
- [x] A per-link override of 10 networks with 6 networks → no alert — `TestPerLinkOverride`
- [x] A muted link with 20 networks → no alert; its page still shows the counts — `TestMutedLinkNoAlert`
- [x] 3 networks at 00:05–00:15 and 2 at 24:30–24:45 (scans every 15 min across the 25 hours) → never more than 3 in a window, no alert — `TestWindowIsTwentyFourHours`
- [x] A disabled link fetched from 6 networks → an alert — `TestDisabledLinkAlerts`
- [x] Two unknown user agents "okhttp/4.12" and "Dalvik/2.1" → 2 apps — `TestUnknownAgentsCountByText`
- [x] A link with no fetches in 24 h → not evaluated (no query result, no event) — `TestQuietLinkNotEvaluated`
- [x] The schedule is declared every 15 minutes; the job, queued and drained, runs the scan and records the alert — `TestSharedScanJob`

Countries, in `alerts/countries_test.go` (an `httptest` lookup server):

- [x] Fetches from a new network queue one lookup job (a second fetch merges into it); the job asks for the network's first address, never a client's, and stores the country — `TestNetworkCountryLookup`
- [x] A failed lookup stores `''`; a fetch from that network queues nothing until `prune` removes the row a day later, and then the next fetch queues a lookup again; the setting empty → no job — `TestFailedLookupRetriesLater`

Pages, in `pages/`:

- [x] After an alert the link page shows the band with today's counts and limits and its actions; muted → no band; "Who fetches it" lists networks with countries and apps over 24 h and 7 d — `link_test.go` `TestLinkAlertPanels`
- [x] Raise limits saves the overrides and records `link.changed{fields: alert limits}`; mute and unmute — `link_test.go` `TestAlertLimitsPage`
- [x] The list marks alerted links, counts them in the status line and filters them with **With alerts** — `links_test.go` `TestLinkListAlerts`
- [x] The dashboard's Links area lists alerted and expiring links; with neither there is no area — `dashboard_test.go` `TestLinksDashboardArea`
- [x] Settings → Subscriptions saves; a URL without `{ip}` or not http(s) is refused inline — `settings_test.go` `TestSubscriptionsSettingsPage`

Notifications and wiring:

## As built

Built 2026-10-08. Every checklist line has its test, in the file the line names (servers' `TestCountrySuggestion` passes from the moved package). `make check` (exit 0), `make lint` (0 issues) and `docker build .` are green; every package of the module runs under `-race`. The pages were also driven in a real Chrome (headless, puppeteer-core, a throwaway site seeded from `substest` on a spare port; nothing committed): the alert band, the 24 h / 7 d switch, **Mute alerts** from the band and **Unmute** from the limits page, the list's marker and **With alerts** chip, the dashboard's Links area, Settings → Subscriptions, the phone width (390 px, no horizontal scroll), no console error or CSP violation. That pass found two layout bugs, both fixed (see below). No real app, ipinfo request or Telegram message was involved: those are the user's. Deviations and notes for 2d and later:

- **Services.** `alerts.New(alerts.Deps{DB, Events, Settings, Jobs, Now, Log})` (`Module.Alerts`); it does not hold `links.Service`: the scan reads link rows through `store`, and `Limits(ctx, links.Link)` takes the link the caller already has. `alerts.FirstAddress(network)` is exported (the address a network is looked up by). `fetch.Deps` gained `Alerts` (nil: no country lookups); `QueueCountry` runs inside the recording transaction, so a failure there loses that fetch's record (logged, the answer still goes out, as in 2b).
- **Store.** `WindowCounts(since, until, linkID)` (0 = every link) is the one grouped count of distinct networks and apps; the scan and the dashboard use it, the link page uses `FetchNetworks`/`FetchApps` (the band's numbers are the lengths of those lists over 24 h). `Fetches` joins `subs_network_countries` (`Fetch.Country`). Also `ExpiredUnmarked`, `ExpiringUnwarned`, `MarkExpired`, `MarkWarned`, `EraseTombstones`, `SetAlertedAt`, `SetAlertLimits`, `PruneFetches`, `PruneCountries`, `HasNetworkCountry`, `NetworksToLookUp`, `PutNetworkCountry`.
- **Times.** The steps take `now` from the module's clock, and their events carry that time (`links.Service.recordAt`). Countries: unknown rows are pruned at `looked_up_at ≤ now − 1 day` (so "a day later" is exact), known ones at 30 days; fetches strictly older than the retention.
- **Notifications.** The module also renders `link.shared_suspected`, so its counts use the language's plural forms ("6 networks and 1 app", RU "из 6 сетей и 1 приложения"); the same plurals are used in the band and the dashboard. Texts as the table says otherwise; RU titles name the link as "Срок ссылки Mom истекает 10 окт".
- **Alert limits page.** `POST /links/:id/alerts` takes `action=mute` / `action=unmute` (the band's **Mute alerts** and the page's **Unmute**, keeping the limits) or the form (`networks`, `apps`: empty = the setting, else 1–1000; `muted=1`). A deleted link answers 409 like every other action. The band's action buttons have their own ids (`alerts.regenerate`, `alerts.disable`) next to the Actions area's.
- **Layout found in the browser.** A row class `app` collided with the shell's `.app` (100 vh rows): "Who fetches it" rows are `.row.who-net` / `.row.who-app`, stacked (networks above apps) because the right column is ~500 px. The fetch log has four columns now: time, **IP · country** (the country under the IP), app, **served · format** (the format under the outcome); five did not fit that column. The list's status column is 150 px so "looks shared" stays on one line.
- **substest.** `StartJobs` (5 ms polls; the scheduler polls hourly, so schedules don't fire in tests), `Drain`, `FetchAt(linkID, at, ip, ua)`.
- **Notes for 2d.** The alert band has room for **Cut off …** between **Disable…** and the spacer (`alertBand` in `link.templ`). `link.cut_off` has no renderer (it doesn't notify).
